0.0.n: This is the character’s name, used here to call him.

0.2.n: An informal call to get someone’s attention.

0.3.n: Repeating ねえ makes the call sound eager and insistent.

0.5.n: Refers to a familiar activity both speakers already know.

0.6.n: The て-form of やる is used alone as a casual request.

1.0.n: The speaker identifies herself as the person to be tossed.

1.1.n: を shows who receives the action of tossing.

1.2.n: The connecting form of 放る combines with 投げる to make 放り投げる, meaning to toss or fling.

1.3.n: The て-form completes 放り投げて and links the tossing to catching.

1.4.n: The borrowed word キャッチ combines with する to work as a verb.

1.5.n: Sentence-ending の explains the activity she means.

2.0.n: An informal response showing recognition and agreement.

2.2.n: Here いい expresses agreement to the request.

2.3.n: ぞ adds firm, masculine-sounding emphasis to his agreement.

2.6.n: 回 counts occurrences; １回 means one turn here.

2.7.n: Distributes the one-turn allowance equally among the children.

2.8.n: Limits the allowance to the amount just stated.

2.9.n: Plain だ finishes the statement after だけ.

2.10.n: ぞ makes the limit sound firm and emphatic.

3.0.n: This is only the first part of そーれ, a call accompanying a physical action.

3.1.n: This mark lengthens the preceding sound in the playful call そーれ.

3.2.n: This completes そーれ; it is not a separate word or a form of る here.

4.0.n: An exclamation of surprise here, not a refusal.

4.2.n: Emphasizes how much the child’s weight has changed.

4.3.n: と follows 随分 to strengthen its description of the degree of change.

4.4.n: 重い changes to 重く before なる to describe becoming heavier.

4.5.n: The past form of なる indicates a change that has already happened.

4.6.n: Casual form of もの, expressing reflective surprise at how things have changed.

4.7.n: Plain だ completes もんだ, giving the observation a reflective tone.

0.lit: Grandpa Pig, hey, hey, do that!
0.tip: A verb’s て-form alone can be a casual request.

1.lit: Toss me and catch me—that’s what you do.
1.tip: The final の explains which activity the child means.

2.lit: Ah, all right! But it is only one time each, mind you.
2.tip: １回ずつだけ combines one time, each, and only to set a one-turn-per-person limit.

3.tip: Treat そーれ as one drawn-out call accompanying the toss, despite the separate word entries.

4.lit: Wow, you have become quite heavy, haven’t you.
4.tip: 重くなった means became heavy; もんだ adds reflective surprise at the change.
